blocks.text: PAGE 1: Why Lists Matter - Your Dashboard Has 10 Lessons From One Array

Hey! In Lesson 3 you learned props + map, in Lesson 6 you filtered lessons with search. Now deep dive into LISTS. Real apps are lists: Your dashboard lessons list, Facebook feed, YouTube videos, Jumia products, WhatsApp chats - all are arrays mapped to components.

Pattern: You have array of data (from Firebase, API, state) -> You map over it -> Return component for each item -> React renders list. But there are traps: Keys, empty lists, loading, no results after search. Today you master all.
Open Practical > React. We build list features your dashboard actually uses.

blocks.text: Remember: map() returns new array. You put {lessons.map(...)} inside JSX {}. For each lesson object, you return <LessonCard /> with props from lesson.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You fetched 20 products from API into products array. How to show ProductCard for each?
options: Write <ProductCard /> 20 times manually
Use products.map(product => <ProductCard key={product.id} {...product} />) - one line renders 20 cards
Use for loop inside JSX directly
You cannot render lists in React
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! map() + key + spread props = standard for all lists. Facebook feed, Jumia, your dashboard all use this.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: map() is the React way: {products.map(p => <ProductCard key={p.id} {...p} />)}. For loop cannot be used directly inside JSX.
blocks.reasoning: map() is fundamental for dynamic lists from API data.

blocks.text: PAGE 3: Keys - Why Your Dashboard Needs Them (Interview Favorite!)

Key is special prop React uses to track which item changed, added, removed. Imagine you have lessons [1,2,3]. You delete lesson 2. Without keys, React doesn't know which one deleted, it may re-render all 3. With keys id=1,2,3, React knows id=2 deleted, only removes that one DOM element - fast!
Rules: Key must be unique among siblings, stable (don't change), and use id from data, NOT index. Index as key causes bugs when you reorder, delete, add.

blocks.output: Both show Intro, JSX but buggy version breaks when deleting/reordering with state inside

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You have todo list with checkbox state inside each TodoItem. You use index as key. User deletes first todo. What bug happens?
options: No bug, index as key works fine always
Checkbox states shift - second todo now shows first todo's checked state because React thinks index 0 is same component, but data changed - keys must be stable id, not index
App crashes
Todos disappear all
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! This is the classic index-as-key bug - state gets mixed when deleting/reordering. Always use id from database!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Index as key bug: When you delete item 0, item 1 becomes index 0, React reuses component with old state. Use id from data as key!
blocks.reasoning: Keys must be stable and unique - id from API, not array index.

blocks.text: PAGE 4: Conditional Rendering - Show Different UI Based on Data

blocks.text: PAGE 5: Empty States, Loading States, No Results - Professional UI

Junior devs only handle happy path - data exists, show list. Senior devs handle all states: Loading (fetching from Firebase - show spinner), Empty (no lessons yet - show 'No lessons, add one'), No Results (search 'xyz' matches 0 - show 'No lessons match xyz'), Error (fetch failed - show retry). Your dashboard HTML has loading spinner and error handling - now you understand why!

blocks.question: APPLICATION: User searches 'Advanced Hooks' but no lesson has that title. What should UI show?
options: Show blank white page - nothing
Show 'No lessons match "Advanced Hooks" - Try different search' with clear button - good UX, not blank
Show error and crash app
Show all lessons ignoring search
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! No results state is crucial UX - don't show blank, show helpful message. Your dashboard should handle this!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Always handle no results: Show message with search term and suggestion. Blank screen confuses users.
blocks.reasoning: Handling all UI states (loading, empty, no results, error) is professional UX.

blocks.question: APPLICATION: You have 10 lessons. You want to show completed lessons first, then current, then locked. How to sort?
options: You cannot sort by status, only by id
Create status order map {completed: 0, current: 1, locked: 2} and sort by that order value: lessons.sort((a,b)=> order[a.status]-order[b.status])
Filter only, cannot sort
Manually reorder array in database
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect! Custom sort with order map - senior dev pattern. Completed first makes sense for user progress!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Map status to number: completed=0, current=1, locked=2, then sort by that number. Custom sorting!
blocks.reasoning: Custom sort logic is common for status-based ordering.

blocks.text: PAGE 8: Performance - Why Keys Matter for Speed

Without keys, when you add one lesson to list of 100, React re-renders all 100 DOM nodes - slow! With keys, React knows only one new id added, it creates one DOM node - fast! Keys help Virtual DOM diffing. Also, avoid anonymous functions inside map for performance in huge lists, but for your 10 lessons it's okay.

blocks.text: PAGE 10: Summary & Next Steps

You mastered: map() to render lists from arrays, keys must be stable unique id not index to avoid state bugs and for performance, conditional rendering 4 patterns (if outside for early return, ternary? : for if-else inside JSX, && for show/hide, object map for many conditions), all UI states (loading spinner while fetching, error with retry, empty with add button, no results with clear filters, happy path list), filtering + sorting + search combined, nested lists (modules -> lessons), and performance with keys helping Virtual DOM diff only changed items.

blocks.question: MASTER APPLICATION: Your dashboard needs to: Show loading while Firebase fetch, if error show retry, if no lessons show 'Add First Lesson', if search matches 0 show 'No results for xyz', otherwise show filtered sorted lessons with correct badge colors. Which pattern?
options: Only map() without any conditions
Early returns for loading/error/empty, then filter + sort, then conditional for no results vs list, ternary for badge colors, && for Start button only if not locked, keys with id
Use only if-else inside map
You need 5 different components for each state
blocks.correctFeedback: PERFECT! You just described production dashboard architecture - early returns + filter/sort + ternary + && + keys. That's exactly how your HTML dashboard works!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Handle all states: if loading return spinner, if error return error, if empty return empty UI, filter, if filtered empty return no results, else map with keys and conditional badge/button.
blocks.reasoning: Handling all list states is what separates junior from senior React dev - your Lesson 10 target needs this.

blocks.question: BUG FIX: You used index as key and have input inside each LessonCard. When you delete lesson 2, input values shift to wrong cards. Why?
options: Because index as key makes React reuse DOM nodes by position, not by id - when you delete index 1, index 2 becomes index 1 but keeps old DOM state
Because React doesn't support inputs in lists
Because you forgot useEffect
Index as key is always correct
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Index bug - React tracks by position not identity. Use stable id from data as key to preserve correct state per item.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Index as key = React thinks position 0 is same component even if data changed. Use id to track identity, not position.
blocks.reasoning: Understanding key bug is crucial for forms inside lists.

blocks.question: When to use && vs ternary? : for conditional rendering?
options: Use && when you want to show something or nothing (show/hide), use ternary when you want to show either A or B (if-else)
They are same, interchangeable always
&& is for loops, ternary for conditions
You should only use if-else outside JSX
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! && = show or hide one thing. Ternary = choose between two things. Your dashboard uses && for Start button, ternary for badge colors.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: &&: {isLoggedIn && <Logout />} - show if true else nothing. Ternary: {status==='completed'? <Completed/> : <Locked/>} - choose one of two.
blocks.reasoning: Choosing right conditional pattern makes code cleaner.
